item.title: [−2] Brent back above $110 as Iran's ship attacks spread beyond Hormuz; settled $108.79 on Tuesday
item.description:
Brent swung from a $111.99 high to settle 0.7% lower on mediation hopes, then rose again. At least 18 vessels were attacked in two weeks. Ongoing near five-month highs.

Aviation, shipping & logistics: headwind (−2) — Jet fuel and freight

Why it matters: Crude at $110 keeps India's import bill, fuel costs and inflation high and pressures the rupee as markets reopen after the holiday.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −2, Inflation outlook −1, Rupee −1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: [−2] Iran says naval mines set two more oil tankers ablaze as attacks spread beyond Hormuz
item.description:
Follows threats to extend its blockade to the Red Sea and Suez. Escalating.

Why it matters: Mines prolong disruption and raise insurance and freight on India's main energy route, keeping delivered crude and LNG costs high.
